ABSTRACT: We have developed a straightforward and rapid methodology for the
synthesis of tetrasubstituted allenes bearing carboxylic acids in the 1,3-position
through the gold(I)-catalyzed nucleophilic addition of bis(trimethylsilyl)ketene
acetals to ynones. The reaction was evaluated with several substrates, and 21 allenes
were obtained in moderate to good yields. Using DFT calculations, we studied the
mechanism of the reaction, which suggested a nucleophilic 1,4-addition pathway.
The potential of allenes to act as a source of highly functionalized lactones was also
explored.
■
INTRODUCTION
Over the years, research on allene chemistry has continuously
grown and evolved, as these compounds are highly versatile
and present in various natural products, bioactive compounds,
and drugs.
1
Allenes are recognized as crucial precursors to
more complex organic compounds.
2
Due to their unique
structure and electronic properties, they have also been object
of study in coordination chemistry
3
and materials science.
4
In recent years, several methodologies for synthesizing
allenes have been developed using transition metal catalyst like
palladium,
5
copper,
6
and gold.
7
In the case of gold, the
transformations generally involve isomerization of propargyl
acetate derivatives, rearrangement of propargyl derivatives, and
S
N
2 reactions.
Although the synthesis of allenes has been widely explored,
8
obtaining tetrasubstituted and highly functionalized allenes is
still a recurrent challenge, in part due to their high reactivity
when the substituents induce intramolecular cyclization.
9
In previous work, when we were studying the reactivity of
ynones toward the nucleophilic addition of bis(trimethylsilyl)-
ketene acetals for the synthesis of 3-hydroxy-pent-4-ynoic
acids, we discovered the formation of the tetrasubstituted
allene 3 as a side product, exclusively when the substituent R
1
in the ynone was p-ClPh, p-MePh, and p-OMePh (Scheme
1).
10
Interestingly, investigations into the electronic properties
of allene 3 (R
1
= p-OMePh, p-MePh) revealed semiconductor
behavior when this phenomenon was investigated over thin
films prepared by vapor deposition of 3 doped with tetracyano-
p-quinodimethane (TCNQ),
4
recently taking advantage of this
property, the preparation of semiconductor membranes
consisting of magnesium phthalocyanine-allene 3 (R = p-
OMePh) particles dispersed in nylon-11 films was explored.
4
Encouraged by these findings, we developed a general
methodology for the synthesis of tetrasubstituted allenes 3,
through the nucleophilic addition of bis(trimethylsilyl)ketene
acetal 2 to ynone 1 catalyzed by AuCI.

According to the DFT calculations, the reaction is proposed
to work via the 1,4-addtion (Figure 2). First, ynone 1 is
activated by the coordination of BF
3
·Et
2
O to the carbonyl
group and the coordination of AuCl to the triple bond, to
generate adduct A. Then, the nucleophilic attack of bis-
(trimethylsilyl)ketene acetal to the activated alkyne in adduct
A proceeds via transition state TS1 with a small energy barrier,
to give the intermediate B, which is 12.8 kcal/mol more stable
than the intermediate C generated by the 1,2-addtion pathway.
A second nucleophilic attack occurs toward the activated
carbonyl group of intermediate B, which is the rate-limiting
reaction step, leading to the formation of the intermediate Y
via the transition state TS2. The energy barrier for this step
was calculated to be 4.5 kcal/mol.
In contrast, for the pathway via 1,2-addition, the trans-
formation of intermediate C to Y requires greater energy,
which is calculated to be 17.9 kcal/mol. Finally, intermediate Y
evolves through an elimination step, leading to Z which easily
hydrolyzes to afford allene 3.
Finally, the reactivity of allene 3n in a cycloisomerization
reaction using CuI (5 mol %) as catalyst in DMF at 100 °C
under microwave irradiation is shown. Z-Lactone 4 was
obtained as a major isomer in 80% yield (Scheme 3).
■
CONCLUSIONS
We developed a general and fast methodology to access highly
functionalized tetrasubstituted allenes 3, through the nucleo-
philic addition of bis(trimethylsilyl)ketene acetals to activated
ynones by a Lewis acid and catalyzed by a commercially
available gold(I) salt under mild conditions. Several ynones
were tested, demonstrating a broad scope of the reaction by
the production of allenes 3 from moderate to good yields, with
the exception of ynones substituted by pyridyl and pyrrolyl,
which did not react. The density functional theory (DFT)
calculations suggested that the mechanism reaction proceeds
via a nucleophilic 1,4-addition, where the first nucleophilic
addition of the bis(trimethylsilyl)ketene acetal to the activated
ynone readily occurs with a low energy barrier, while addition
of the second molecule of bis(trimethylsilyl)ketene is the rate
limiting step. The reactivity of allene 3n was demonstrated by a
cycloisomerization reaction, showing the potential of these
substrates as precursors of highly functionalized lactones.
